page: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v7 is a compute-oriented virtual machine instance powered by the Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled on a Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz and features a substantial 480 MB L3 cache. It is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, providing 236 GB of disk capacity, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPUs are included.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression reaching 36.23 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.92 GB/sec. However, multi-core and multi-threaded scaling is relatively weak, as seen in the stress-ng multi-core score of 4655.9 and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression of 29.51 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is average for read operations, peaking at 345.13 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 43.66 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, but drops to a weak 23.53 GB/sec for large block writes. Passmark CPU and memory scores sit in the average tier, as do Redis SET operations at 8.31 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 8.67 GB/sec. Large-model LLM inference is poor, with a 7B model achieving only 4.86 tokens/sec for text generation.

Given its low memory-to-core ratio, the D4lds_v7 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The inclusion of 236 GB of local storage and Premium Storage capability adds value for IO-sensitive tasks. It is best suited for single-threaded applications, lightweight web serving, basic database operations, and entry-level compute tasks. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, heavy multi-threaded parallel processing, or large-scale machine learning inference.
